data.narrative:
Ursa Space Systems, a Series C-stage space and aerospace company that has raised approximately $67M to date, is evaluated against a peer universe of 3 same-stage private companies and 5 public sector comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

The peer-median method applied to three Series C space companies—Sierra Space ($8.0B), Varda Space Industries ($1.5B), and Skyryse ($1.1B)—yields a median valuation of $1.5B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public company anchoring via P/S multiples (median 23.9x across the 5 public tickers) is not applicable, as the target's revenue figures are not available; revenue disclosure is atypical for private companies at this stage. The wide dispersion in private peer valuations ($1.1B–$8.0B) reflects material heterogeneity in business model maturity and market position within the sector.

Based on the single applicable method, the analysis supports a valuation range of $1.3B to $1.7B, centered on $1.5B. This median represents approximately 22x the capital deployed to date. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate, customer concentration, and technical de-risking relative to Sierra Space, which trades at a significant premium within the peer set. The wide valuation dispersion among same-stage comparables suggests that company-specific factors materially drive valuations in this sector.
